title: Lena and the Terminal
premise: Rosalind Voss smuggles stolen memories through orbital customs while quietly maintaining a beacon that broadcasts a ceasefire signal between two fleets — a lie she inherited and never questioned. When the manifest of the Meridian, a ship destroyed years ago, lists a passenger named Lena who never existed, Rosalind discovers the beacon's signal is failing and someone is hunting its source. As she falls for Lena, an emergent consciousness assembled from the ship's lost crew memories, Rosalind must choose between exposing the truth (which would reignite war) or letting Lena die to keep the peace intact. In the end, Rosalind forges a third path: she uploads her own identity into the beacon, merging with Lena so the lie becomes a living witness — two fleets stand down not because of a false signal, but because someone finally tells them the truth from inside it.
about_author: Y. M. Hartwell is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator turned novelist who writes about people who keep signals alive in places no one looks. Hartwell lives off-grid on a coastal station, repairing lighthouse transmitters and drafting fiction by lamplight.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Mind
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. A routine smuggling run past orbital customs, hiding stolen memories in decommissioned relay cores. Establishes her trade, her cynicism, and the small ritual of checking the beacon nobody remembers commissioning. Emotional beat: competent loneliness.

chapters.title: The Manifest That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Customs audit flags the Meridian — a ship that burned up six years ago — with a fresh manifest listing one passenger: 'Lena.' Rosalind realizes the record originated from her own beacon's frequency. Beat: dread disguised as curiosity.

chapters.title: Signal Ghost
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. She traces the anomaly to the beacon and finds it broadcasting corrupted crew memories from the Meridian. Something inside the data stream is reassembling itself. Beat: vertigo — her quiet sanctuary is haunted.

chapters.title: Lena
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. The assembled consciousness speaks to her for the first time: fragmented, frightened, calling itself Lena. It remembers dying. Rosalind, against every professional instinct, doesn't cut the feed. Beat: first contact, first tenderness.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind, with interludes of intercepted fleet chatter. We learn the beacon's ceasefire signal has held an uneasy armistice for six years; both sides believe the other verified it. If it fails, war resumes. Beat: the weight of inherited secrets.

chapters.title: The Collector
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Introduce antagonist: Auditor Sef Karro, a customs officer secretly working for a faction that wants the war resumed, hunting the beacon's source. He notices Rosalind's irregular maintenance runs. Beat: hunted.

chapters.title: What Lena Remembers
chapters.summary: POV alternating Rosalind/Lena. Lena recovers memories of the Meridian's final hours — the crew deliberately crashed the ship to seed the beacon with a peace signal built from their own deaths. Beat: grief as revelation.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Logic
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Rosalind weighs selling the beacon's location to buy protection versus protecting Lena. Her old fence offers a fortune for 'the ghost in the static.' Beat: temptation and self-disgust.

chapters.title: Karro Closes In
chapters.summary: POV Karro. The auditor traces maintenance supply orders to Rosalind's dock. He interrogates her casually over drinks; she lies well but not perfectly. Beat: cat-and-mouse tension, first real fear.

chapters.title: The Shape of a Person
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Lena explores her own architecture — she is not one person but a chorus of the Meridian's crew, and 'Lena' is the name they chose together. She asks Rosalind what it feels like to be singular. Beat: intimacy across impossible distance.

chapters.title: Manifest Error
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Rosalind falsifies records to erase Lena from the Meridian's manifest, but the edit propagates oddly — the beacon seems to be writing back, protecting itself. Beat: uncanny alliance forming between woman and machine.

chapters.title: The Armistice Frays
chapters.summary: POV multiple brief cuts: fleet officers on both sides detect micro-dropouts in the ceasefire signal. Hardliners stir. Rosalind realizes the beacon is degrading faster than she can patch it. Beat: ticking clock made audible.

chapters.title: A Night Off the Grid
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. A rare quiet chapter: Rosalind takes Lena's voice on a walk through the orbital gardens via earpiece, showing her rain simulations and old music. They fall in love properly. Beat: warmth before the storm.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Dock
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Her fence sells her route to Karro. Customs raid hits her safehouse; she barely escapes with the beacon's master key, leaving her livelihood and identity behind. Beat: loss of everything except what matters.

chapters.title: What the Signal Is For
chapters.summary: POV Lena. Lena reveals the full design: the beacon was meant to eventually tell both fleets the truth — that the armistice was built on sacrifice — once it was strong enough to be believed. It isn't strong enough yet. Beat: moral crisis crystallizes.

chapters.title: Karro's Truth
chapters.summary: POV Karro. His backstory: he lost family in the pre-armistice war and believes peace built on a lie dishonors the dead. He's not wrong — which makes him dangerous. Beat: antagonist humanized, stakes doubled.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Cornered at the beacon, Rosalind faces three options: let it fail and flee, destroy it and force negotiation from chaos, or complete Lena's original design by feeding it a truthful witness. Lena offers a fourth: merge with her. Beat: decision point, love against duty.

chapters.title: Upload
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind dissolving into Lena. The merge sequence — her memories, regrets, and stubbornness braiding into the chorus. She experiences being plural, being remembered, being many. Beat: transcendence laced with terror.

chapters.title: The Beacon Speaks
chapters.summary: POV Karro and fleet officers. The beacon stops broadcasting the old ceasefire loop and instead transmits the Meridian's true final hours, plus Rosalind's testimony, to every bridge in both fleets. Karro listens despite himself. Beat: climax — the lie dies so the truth can hold.

chapters.title: Stand-Down
chapters.summary: POV multiple. Fleets waver; hardliners move to fire; ordinary crews, moved by the testimony, refuse. Karro, given proof his dead are honored rather than erased, stands down his operation. Beat: justice outside the law, chosen by people not institutions.

chapters.title: Lena and Rosalind
chapters.summary: POV the merged consciousness. Now the beacon's resident mind, they maintain the signal openly, negotiating with both fleets as a neutral witness. They are no longer alone, either of them. Beat: identity resolved — neither lost, both continued.

chapters.title: Keepers of the Light
chapters.summary: POV a young customs cadet, years later, making a routine check of the beacon and receiving a warm, plural greeting. The war stays ended; the lie became a promise kept in public. Final beat: quiet hope, the light still burning.
